title: July Membership Luncheon
summary: Monthly member lunch with a legislative update from the Georgia Chamber's west Georgia field office.
description:
Join us for our monthly membership luncheon at the Bremen Civic Center. This month's speaker is the Georgia Chamber's west Georgia field director with a mid-year legislative update — what passed this session, what it means for small business, and what's coming in 2027.

Lunch is catered by The Mill Table. Doors open at 11:15 for networking; the program starts at noon sharp so you're back at work by 1.

Bring plenty of business cards — we'll do our 60-second member introductions before the program.

title: Ribbon Cutting: Ridgeline Fitness Expansion
summary: Celebrate the grand opening of Ridgeline Fitness's new group class wing — big scissors, door prizes, and smoothies.
description:
Help us celebrate the grand opening of Ridgeline Fitness's new 3,000-square-foot group class wing! The big scissors come out at 10am sharp, followed by facility tours, door prizes, and smoothie samples from the new juice bar.

Ribbon cuttings are free and open to everyone — members, neighbors, and anyone curious. Come show a growing local business some hometown support.

title: Business After Hours at Little River Farms
summary: Casual evening networking in the event barn — heavy hors d'oeuvres, farm tours at sunset, and zero PowerPoints.
description:
Our quarterly Business After Hours heads to the event barn at Little River Farms. No programs, no slides — just two hours to actually talk with other business owners over heavy hors d'oeuvres and sweet tea (and a cash bar).

The Hembree family is offering wagon tours of the farm at sunset for anyone who wants one. Dress is casual; the barn is climate controlled but it's August, so plan accordingly.

First-time attendees get a yellow name tag so folks know to come say hello. Don't be shy.

title: Workshop: Marketing Your Business Without a Marketing Budget
venue: West Georgia Technical College, Murphy Campus
summary: Hands-on workshop covering Google Business Profiles, Facebook that works, and getting reviews — laptops welcome.
description:
A practical, hands-on morning for owners who do their own marketing. We'll cover claiming and polishing your Google Business Profile, a Facebook posting rhythm that doesn't eat your week, and how to ask for reviews without feeling awkward.

Bring a laptop if you can — the second half is a working session where you'll fix your own listings on the spot with help in the room. Coffee and biscuits provided by Tallapoosa Coffee Co. and Sweetwater Bakery.

Seats are limited to 40 so everyone gets help. UGA Small Business Development Center consultants will stick around after for one-on-one questions.

title: Fall Festival on the Square — Downtown Tallapoosa
summary: 100+ vendors, live music on two stages, a kids' zone, and the famous chamber funnel cake booth.
description:
The Fall Festival returns to downtown Tallapoosa with more than 100 craft and food vendors, live music on two stages, a classic car cruise-in, and a kids' zone on Lyon Street. The chamber funnel cake booth — staffed by your board of directors in aprons — benefits the Haralson Youth Sports Foundation.

Admission and parking are free. Shuttles run from the First Baptist and city hall lots every 15 minutes.

Vendor booths are sold out, but food truck spots remain — contact the chamber office if you're interested.

title: 28th Annual Chamber Golf Classic
summary: Four-person scramble benefiting the Haralson Youth Sports Foundation — lunch, prizes, and the $10,000 hole-in-one.
description:
Our biggest fundraiser of the year: a four-person scramble at Maple Creek with breakfast at registration, lunch on the turn from Big Creek BBQ, and an awards reception to follow. Every dollar of net proceeds goes to the Haralson Youth Sports Foundation — last year's tournament put 340 kids on a field.

Prizes for first, last, longest drive, and closest to the pin, plus the $10,000 hole-in-one challenge on 17, sponsored by Haralson Insurance Agency.

Team registration is $400 and includes carts, meals, and swag bags. Hole sponsorships from $150 — a great way to get your logo in front of 120 golfers who own businesses.
